```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      dev = "svg")
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

# Settings

Edit this chunk to change the positivity rule. Nothing is excluded from the
pipeline outputs: this report labels, it does not filter.

Detection is reported in two tiers, because a single threshold cannot handle
both arms of this reference. An RNA virus present as an infection covers much
of its genome. A DNA virus such as a herpesvirus is detected here through
transcription, so coverage concentrates on a few transcribed genes and breadth
stays low however real the signal. The confident tier is what the data can
support on its own; the suggestive tier is what needs a coverage profile
before it can be called either way.

```{r thresholds}
# Confident tier: all three must hold
tier1_min_reads <- 10
tier1_min_breadth <- 0.10        # covered bases over reference length
tier1_min_windows_fraction <- 0.30

# Suggestive tier: enough reads to be worth inspecting, but failing the above
tier2_min_reads <- 100

# Blank comparison. A taxon must exceed this multiple of its RPM in the blank.
# Taxa absent from the blank pass automatically.
blank_ratio_min <- 10

# Which RPM is used for the blank comparison and the headline figures.
# "rpm_total"   per million reads surviving trimming
# "rpm_nonhost" per million reads STAR could not place
# The two differ by an order of magnitude here, because the non-host fraction
# ranges from 2.5% to 97%. Whichever is chosen must be named in the methods.
rpm_metric <- "rpm_total"

# Group label marking the negative controls in the sample sheet
blank_prefix <- "blank"
```

```{r read_inputs}
out_step <- file.path(params$out_dir, "04_viral")
counts_dir <- file.path(out_step, "counts")

samples_meta <- read_tsv(params$sample_sheet, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(any_of(c("sample_id", "body_site", "group", "batch")))

if ("body_site" %in% names(samples_meta)) {
  samples_meta <- samples_meta |>
    mutate(body_site = str_to_lower(str_trim(body_site)))
}

per_taxid <- read_tsv(file.path(counts_dir, "viral_per_taxid.tsv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)
denominators <- read_tsv(file.path(counts_dir, "viral_denominators.tsv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE)

is_blank <- function(x) !is.na(x) & str_starts(x, blank_prefix)

# windows_fraction is written by merge_viral.py; recomputed here if an older
# output is being read
if (!"windows_fraction" %in% names(per_taxid)) {
  per_taxid <- per_taxid |>
    mutate(windows_total = pmax(1, ceiling(total_ref_length / 1000)),
           windows_fraction = windows_covered / windows_total)
}

detections <- per_taxid |>
  mutate(rpm_used = .data[[rpm_metric]]) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

blank_samples <- detections |>
  filter(is_blank(group)) |>
  pull(sample_id) |>
  unique()
```

# Denominators

The two RPM denominators disagree sharply here, so any abundance figure has to
say which it uses. The non-host fraction is what module 01 could not place on
the human genome, and it ranges widely across these samples.

```{r denominators_table}
denominators |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id") |>
  transmute(
    sample = sample_id,
    site = if ("body_site" %in% names(samples_meta)) body_site else NA,
    group = if ("group" %in% names(samples_meta)) group else NA,
    `trimmed pairs (M)` = round(trimmed_pairs / 1e6, 1),
    `non-host pairs (M)` = round(nonhost_pairs / 1e6, 1),
    `non-host %` = round(100 * nonhost_fraction, 1)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

# The noise floor, measured on the blank

Every taxon the negative control picks up is noise by construction, so the
blank tells us what spurious assignment looks like in these libraries rather
than our having to guess.

```{r blank_profile}
if (length(blank_samples) == 0) {
  cat("No blank controls in the sample sheet; the blank comparison below is skipped.\n")
} else {
  detections |>
    filter(sample_id %in% blank_samples) |>
    arrange(desc(reads)) |>
    transmute(
      sample = sample_id,
      taxon = virus_name,
      family,
      `ref length (kb)` = round(total_ref_length / 1000, 1),
      reads,
      `breadth %` = round(100 * breadth, 2),
      windows = str_c(windows_covered, " / ", windows_total),
      `windows frac` = round(windows_fraction, 3),
      rpm = round(rpm_used, 2)
    ) |>
    head(20) |>
    kable(caption = "Highest-count taxa in the negative control")
}
```

```{r blank_ceiling}
if (length(blank_samples) > 0) {
  blank_rows <- filter(detections, sample_id %in% blank_samples)
  tibble(
    metric = c("taxa detected", "max reads", "max breadth %",
               "max windows fraction"),
    value = c(
      as.character(nrow(blank_rows)),
      format(max(blank_rows$reads), big.mark = ","),
      sprintf("%.2f", 100 * max(blank_rows$breadth)),
      sprintf("%.3f", max(blank_rows$windows_fraction))
    )
  ) |>
    kable(caption = "Ceiling observed in the blank")
}
```

# Where the thresholds fall

Each point is one taxon in one sample. The blank's taxa are drawn separately,
so the thresholds can be read against the measured noise rather than against
an assumption.

```{r threshold_plot, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5}
plot_data <- detections |>
  mutate(source = if_else(sample_id %in% blank_samples,
                          "negative control", "sample"))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = windows_fraction, y = breadth, size = reads,
                      colour = source)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tier1_min_breadth, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = tier1_min_windows_fraction, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log10", labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("sample" = "#2b6cb0",
                                 "negative control" = "#c53030")) +
  labs(x = "Fraction of reference windows covered",
       y = "Breadth (covered bases over reference length)",
       size = "Reads", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The top right quadrant is the confident tier. Points far left with high read
counts are the pattern to be wary of: many reads stacked on one short stretch
of the reference.

```{r distributions}
detections |>
  summarise(
    `taxon-sample rows` = n(),
    `median reads` = median(reads),
    `p90 reads` = quantile(reads, 0.90),
    `median breadth %` = round(100 * median(breadth), 2),
    `p99 breadth %` = round(100 * quantile(breadth, 0.99), 2),
    `rows breadth >= 10%` = sum(breadth >= tier1_min_breadth),
    `rows windows frac >= 0.3` = sum(windows_fraction >= tier1_min_windows_fraction)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  kable(caption = "Distribution across all taxon-sample rows")
```

# Detections

```{r calls}
blank_rpm <- detections |>
  filter(sample_id %in% blank_samples) |>
  group_by(virus_taxid) |>
  summarise(blank_rpm = max(rpm_used), .groups = "drop")

calls <- detections |>
  filter(!sample_id %in% blank_samples) |>
  left_join(blank_rpm, by = "virus_taxid") |>
  mutate(
    blank_rpm = replace_na(blank_rpm, 0),
    blank_ratio = if_else(blank_rpm > 0, rpm_used / blank_rpm, NA_real_),
    passes_blank = is.na(blank_ratio) | blank_ratio >= blank_ratio_min,
    meets_tier1 = reads >= tier1_min_reads &
      breadth >= tier1_min_breadth &
      windows_fraction >= tier1_min_windows_fraction,
    tier = case_when(
      meets_tier1 & passes_blank  ~ "confident",
      meets_tier1 & !passes_blank ~ "confident but blank-matched",
      reads >= tier2_min_reads    ~ "suggestive, needs coverage check",
      TRUE                        ~ "below thresholds"
    )
  )
```

## Confident tier

```{r tier1_table}
tier1 <- calls |> filter(str_starts(tier, "confident"))

if (nrow(tier1) == 0) {
  cat("No taxon met the confident tier.\n")
} else {
  tier1 |>
    arrange(sample_id, desc(reads)) |>
    transmute(
      sample = sample_id,
      site = if ("body_site" %in% names(calls)) body_site else NA,
      taxon = virus_name,
      genus,
      family,
      reads,
      `breadth %` = round(100 * breadth, 1),
      `windows frac` = round(windows_fraction, 2),
      rpm = round(rpm_used, 1),
      `blank ratio` = if_else(is.na(blank_ratio), "absent from blank",
                              as.character(round(blank_ratio, 1))),
      tier
    ) |>
    kable()
}
```

## Suggestive tier

Enough reads to be worth inspecting, but failing breadth or spread. These are
not detections. A coverage profile distinguishes the two explanations: reads
concentrated on a few separated regions is what transcription of a large DNA
virus looks like, while a single narrow spike is what cross-mapping looks like.

```{r tier2_table}
tier2 <- calls |> filter(tier == "suggestive, needs coverage check")

if (nrow(tier2) == 0) {
  cat("Nothing in the suggestive tier.\n")
} else {
  tier2 |>
    arrange(desc(reads)) |>
    transmute(
      sample = sample_id,
      taxon = virus_name,
      family,
      `ref length (kb)` = round(total_ref_length / 1000, 1),
      reads,
      reads_hiq,
      `breadth %` = round(100 * breadth, 2),
      windows = str_c(windows_covered, " / ", windows_total),
      `windows frac` = round(windows_fraction, 3),
      rpm = round(rpm_used, 1)
    ) |>
    head(30) |>
    kable()
}
```

# Taxa flagged in the reference

Sequences marked `contamination-prone` when the reference set was built,
chiefly XMRV and murine leukemia virus. They are kept in the index so such
reads land where they belong rather than being pushed onto other taxa. A hit
here is never a finding without separate verification.

```{r flagged}
flagged <- calls |> filter(!is.na(flags), flags != "")

if (nrow(flagged) == 0) {
  cat("No flagged taxon was detected in any sample.\n")
} else {
  flagged |>
    arrange(desc(reads)) |>
    transmute(sample = sample_id, taxon = virus_name, flags, reads,
              `breadth %` = round(100 * breadth, 2),
              `windows frac` = round(windows_fraction, 3),
              rpm = round(rpm_used, 2), tier) |>
    kable()
}
```

# Family-level summary

Strain-level assignment is unreliable when the reference holds many
near-identical genomes per family, so reads are aggregated. A single infection
typically appears as reads spread across many references of one family, which
is why the family total is firmer than any individual row above.

```{r family_summary}
calls |>
  group_by(family) |>
  summarise(
    `taxa detected` = n_distinct(virus_taxid),
    `total reads` = sum(reads),
    `samples with any` = n_distinct(sample_id),
    `confident calls` = sum(str_starts(tier, "confident")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(`total reads`)) |>
  kable()
```

# Sensitivity note: anelloviruses

Anelloviruses are near-ubiquitous in healthy people, so their detection was
intended as a check that this arm works. Two caveats apply before the numbers
are read that way. They are DNA viruses, so in an RNA library they appear only
through transcription and a non-transcribing carrier looks negative. And they
are among the most diverse virus families known, while the reference holds one
genome per taxon, so a divergent strain is expected to match only its most
conserved region.

```{r anellovirus}
anello <- calls |> filter(family == "Anelloviridae")

if (nrow(anello) == 0) {
  cat("No anellovirus reads in any sample. Read as a sensitivity flag, not a finding.\n")
} else {
  anello |>
    group_by(sample_id) |>
    summarise(
      `taxa with reads` = n(),
      `total reads` = sum(reads),
      `max breadth %` = round(100 * max(breadth), 2),
      `max windows frac` = round(max(windows_fraction), 3),
      `any confident` = any(str_starts(tier, "confident")),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    kable(caption = "Anellovirus reads per sample")
}
```

Presence of reads is not the same as a confirmed detection. If breadth stays
low, the coverage profile is what separates a divergent real strain from
cross-mapping, and `scripts/viral_taxon_diagnostic.sh` is the tool for that.

# Outputs written

```{r write_out}
if (isTRUE(params$write_calls_tsv)) {
  out_file <- file.path(counts_dir, "viral_calls.tsv")
  calls |>
    select(sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group")), virus_taxid, virus_name,
           genus, family, category, flags, reads, reads_hiq, covered_bases,
           total_ref_length, breadth, windows_covered, windows_total,
           windows_fraction, rpm_total, rpm_nonhost, blank_rpm, blank_ratio,
           passes_blank, tier) |>
    write_tsv(out_file)
  cat("Calls written to:", out_file, "\n")
}
```

# Notes

- This report labels; it never filters a pipeline output. `viral_calls.tsv`
  carries every taxon-sample row with its tier.
- Thresholds in force: `r tier1_min_reads` reads,
  `r 100 * tier1_min_breadth`% breadth and
  `r tier1_min_windows_fraction` windows fraction for the confident tier;
  `r tier2_min_reads` reads for the suggestive tier; blank ratio
  `r blank_ratio_min`. They were set from this pilot's distribution and should
  be revisited when the cohort arrives.
- Abundance here uses `r rpm_metric`. The two denominators differ by an order
  of magnitude in these samples because the non-host fraction ranges from
  2.5% to 97%, so the choice belongs in the methods.
- `windows_fraction` is used rather than the raw window count because the
  latter is not comparable across genome sizes: the same count is most of a
  7 kb enterovirus and a few percent of a 472 kb herpesvirus.
- Herpesviruses in an RNA library are lytic transcription, not genome load.
  That is a different claim from presence of the virus and should be worded as
  such.
- GRCh38 sits in the same index as a decoy. A large share of the reads STAR
  could not place map back to human under local alignment, and without the
  decoy they would have been forced onto viral genomes instead.
